MacPaw announces long-term strategic partnership with Liquid AI to jointly develop a Mac-exclusive on-device AI technology stack.

The collaboration will begin with Eney, the macOS AI assistant developed by MacPaw.

MacPaw and Liquid AI partner to bring more on-device AI capabilities to Mac

Liquid AI's Liquid Foundation Models (LFMs) will be tailored for Mac assistant scenarios and integrated with MacPaw's proprietary on-device technologies: Mnemos, which handles memory, and Elix, which handles reasoning.

Eney switched to local models as early as last year, keeping inference, contextual search, skill execution and conversation history processed on-device as much as possible.

This new partnership aims to further advance this direction. The two companies are jointly developing the underlying technology stack, rather than simply having MacPaw add another third-party model.

MacPaw stated that once the technology is tested and implemented on Eney, it plans to extend it to more of its products. They also hope to open the shared AI technology stack to Mac developers through Setapp.

This way, participating applications can share more functionality and contextual information with Eney, allowing the assistant to understand content within applications, thereby providing more useful answers or performing relevant actions.

To learn more about MacPaw's on-device AI technology and today's announcement, please visit here; you can also follow Liquid AI's latest developments here.
